mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year increase in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) exceeding 3% signals stronger household demand, which boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods of GDPC1 growth > 3% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 6-month decline in the unemployment rate below 4% indicates a tight labor market, which raises wage pressure and inflation expectations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as discount rates rise.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods of UNRATE < 4% for 6 months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) exceeding 2% signals weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate earnings and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods of INDPRO 3-month change < -2% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both the federal funds rate and CPI inflation above 3% signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, which increases discount rates and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods of FEDFUNDS > 3% AND CPIAUCSL > 3% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 6-month decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) exceeding 2% signals weakening household demand, which reduces corporate earnings and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods of GDPC1 6-month change < -2% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month increase in the unemployment rate above 0.5% signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods of UNRATE 3-month change > 0.5% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 6-month increase in the industrial production index (INDPRO) exceeding 4% signals a strong manufacturing rebound, which boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods of INDPRO 6-month change > 4% (t-test p > 0.05).
